contradicting_evidence: BTC and ETH remain positive in the supplied daily proxy snapshot and latest completed hour; weak alt participation does not by itself imply an absolute market decline.
The 90-day BlockchainCenter sample has positive median alt returns despite underperformance versus BTC, so the longer-window evidence is not uniformly contractionary.
The structural prior records an earlier positive BTC settled-flow aggregate. The latest negative session challenges that support but does not establish a durable reversal in institutional demand.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: An uneven downside bias remains the better-supported weekly hypothesis if liquidity contraction and weak participation persist. Stabilization attempts may interrupt weakness, with BTC/ETH potentially more resilient than the observed alt proxies. A sustained recovery requires new confirmation; neither a cycle transition nor microcap direction can be inferred.
falsification_conditions: Stablecoin supply contraction gives way to sustained expansion, accompanied by evidence of deployment and persistent improvement in market participation.
Successive settled ETF observations improve while BTC/ETH gains hold and ETH/BTC strengthens, weakening the demand-contraction thesis.
Broad proxy participation and median returns improve persistently rather than gains remaining concentrated in a few constituents.
missing_evidence: A week-spanning price and participation sequence to distinguish a durable trend from a temporary rebound.
New settled ETF sessions and stablecoin observations confirming whether current demand headwinds persist.
Updated macro direction and usable catalyst context across the forecast window.
Canonical rotation confirmation and any evidence covering the unavailable microcap universe.
supporting_evidence: Stablecoin supply is down approximately 1.37% over seven days and 2.66% over 30 days. This is a broader liquidity headwind, although supply changes do not directly measure deployed buying power.
The latest final ETF session shows outflows for both BTC and ETH, reducing support for extrapolating earlier BTC-flow resilience into the coming week.

The 30-day BlockchainCenter score is 24, with only 12 of 49 constituents outperforming BTC and a negative median alt return. This supports weak recent alt participation, not a standalone forecast of absolute market decline.
Current breadth and capitalization proxies do not show a broadening recovery capable of offsetting the observed liquidity headwinds.
